query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount of aluminum (on the order of 1–3 atomic %) to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will enhance its oxygen resistance during high‐temperature exposure by promoting the formation of an adherent, slow‐growing alumina (Al2O3) scale while preserving its room-temperature ductility and high‐temperature yield strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr, which exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C, but suffers from inadequate oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Minor alloying addition of aluminum (1–3 at%) into the HfNbTaTiZr composition.
generation.conditions: Exposure in air at elevated temperatures (e.g., 800–1000 °C) for durations on the order of 5 hours under nominal mechanical loading conditions, as well as standard room-temperature tensile and high-temperature yield tests.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous and adherent Al2O3 scale on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: Aluminum is a strong oxide former. When a minor amount is added, it oxidizes preferentially to form a dense, protective alumina scale. This scale acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, thereby slowing down internal oxidation (pesting) without substantially altering the matrix microstructure that governs ductility and yield strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated material, the Al-doped alloy should show significantly lower oxidation kinetics (reduced oxygen uptake and pesting) at 800–1000 °C while retaining similar room-temperature ductility (within the 8–16% range) and high-temperature yield strength.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits inadequate oxygen resistance despite its useful mechanical performance (8–16% ductility at room temperature and 163–530 MPa yield strength at 1000 °C).
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected when the aluminum addition is kept low (1–3 at%) so as not to induce new phases or substantially alter the solid solution microstructure; tests are bounded to exposure in air at 800–1000 °C for ~5 hours and standard mechanical testing conditions.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the precise Al content that optimizes the balance between improved oxidation resistance and retained mechanical performance, and the potential influence of Al on phase stability requires further evaluation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of cast HfNbTaTiZr samples: one set modified with 1–3 at% aluminum and one set as the unmodified reference. Expose both sets to air at 800–1000 °C for 5 hours under identical conditions. After exposure, evaluate the surface oxide scale via microscopy and measure the weight gain due to oxidation. Additionally, perform room-temperature tensile tests and high-temperature (e.g., 1000 °C) yield strength measurements to assess if mechanical properties remain within acceptable ranges.
measurements: Weight gain per unit area and oxide scale morphology and adherence (via SEM/XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-modified alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in oxidation (lower weight gain and formation of a continuous, adherent alumina scale) compared to the reference, or if its room-temperature ductility and/or high-temperature yield strength degrade by more than approximately 10% relative to the baseline alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.
